_README: Machine-readable ledger of client-model fidelity GAPS. Each language key maps to a list of JSON paths (dot notation; '*' = any array index) that the client's Expectation model currently DROPS or MUTATES on a JSON round-trip, so its round-trip fidelity test can excuse exactly those paths and land green today. This file is the backlog for the model-completion wave: when a client model is fixed to carry a field, REMOVE its path here and the per-client test's ratchet re-arms the assertion (a stale entry that no longer excuses any diff fails CI). Keys beginning with '_' are metadata and are ignored by tests. See .opencode (roundtrip-spec) / the per-client test headers for the exact comparator algorithm. php has verbatim rawData replay, so it has zero gaps. NOTE: 'node' entries document the generated mockServer.d.ts TYPE gaps enforced at compile time via isolated // @ts-expect-error markers in test/roundtrip_fidelity_types.ts (the type test does NOT read this file); removing a .d.ts gap makes its marker unused and fails tsc. 'php' is empty because the PHP client replays decoded JSON verbatim.
_notation: segment.segment ; array index as a literal index in a diff but written as '*' here so entries are fixture-length independent. A shorter entry excuses its whole subtree.
_go_note: httpRequest.pathParameters is a pre-existing model limitation, not a droppable field: HttpRequest.PathParametersList is typed map[string][]string and the public builder RequestBuilder.PathParameter(name string, values ...string) writes into it, but the schema-matcher wire form is { name: [ { schema: {...} } ] }, which []string cannot hold. Widening the field (or the builder) to carry schema objects is a breaking type/signature change, disallowed by the additive-only contract, so this one path is retained. All other go gaps were closed by additively adding typed fields.
